text:
The rhythm of the rails was a metronome for Mira’s unraveling sanity. *Clack-clack, clack-clack.* The world blurred into streaks of rusted iron and overgrown briar, but the station remained sharp, etched in gray concrete against the fading twilight.

First day: one suitcase. Brown leather, scuffed at the corners, standing alone like a tombstone.
Second day: two suitcases. A black valise added to the first, zipped tight, holding secrets no one would ever unpack.
Third day: three. A battered canvas bag with fraying straps, leaking hope onto the dusty tiles.

Mira pressed her forehead against the cold glass, breath fogging the view. Each passing train brought another piece of luggage, accumulating in silent judgment. Who packed them? Why here? The abandoned platform had become a museum of departures, each case a frozen moment of hesitation before someone chose not to board.

By the seventh pass, seven suitcases lined the edge, teetering precariously near the tracks. They seemed to lean inward, conspiring. Mira watched, heart hammering against her ribs, waiting for the eighth. She wondered if she should stop the train, step out, and open them all. Or perhaps she was already inside one, packed away by time, watching herself from behind the glass as the next suitcase appeared, waiting patiently for its owner to finally arrive.
